title: Hyperscalers Raise $271B in Global Debt This Year to Fund AI Spending

tickers.name: Alphabet Inc. Class A Common Stock
Meta Platforms, Inc. Class A Common Stock

summary:
The combined global debt issuance from Alphabet, Amazon, Microsoft, Meta, and Oracle has climbed to $271 billion this year as the companies borrow heavily to fund artificial intelligence infrastructure. This latest total follows a burst of activity between Oct. 29 and Nov. 3, during which the hyperscaler group raised $41.7 billion across three separate bond deals.

The spending binge helped push year-to-date US investment-grade bond sales to a record $1.76 trillion, exceeding the previous pandemic-era peak of $1.75 trillion set in 2020. European Central Bank President Christine Lagarde said this volume of issuance from hyperscalers has played a role in rising bond yields, even as total global bond sales hit an all-time high of $6.61 trillion. Bank of America forecasts that the trend will peak in November with an estimated $175 billion in US investment-grade issuance, which would be the highest for any November on record.

selectedTweets.text:
US corporate debt issuance is skyrocketing:

US investment-grade corporate bond sales are expected to rise +$37 billion YoY in November, or +27%, to $175 billion, the highest for any November on record.

This would mark a +$76 billion, or +77%, increase from November 2024 level.

To put this into perspective, the 5-year average before 2025 was $104 billion.

By comparison, US investment-grade bond issuance stood at ~$100 billion in October.

As a result, US investment-grade bond sales have risen to a record $1.76 trillion YTD, already surpassing the full-year 2025 total of $1.75 trillion.

Meanwhile, over $300 billion in AI-related corporate bonds have been issued in global investment-grade markets so far in 2026, almost 3 times the total for all of 2025.

AI spending is fueling an unprecedented wave of corporate borrowing.
